cards.back: Obvious visual peaks or valleys where price hits a barrier of strong buyers or sellers and undergoes a drastic reversal.
The principle that larger timeframe structures consistently overpower smaller timeframe noise because creating them requires significantly more money and volume.
A systematic three-step process requiring traders to identify the 4-hour trend, wait for 1-hour structure, and verify 15-minute alignment before execution.
A non-negotiable requirement that the entry timeframe must build structure in the exact same direction as the overarching 1-hour and 4-hour trends.
The rapid acceleration of price that occurs after breaking resistance when no historical sellers are present to block the movement.
Established zones of historical buyers or sellers that act as obstacles, causing high-speed price momentum to stall or reverse.
A disciplined mindset focused on waiting for high-probability setups with perfect multi-timeframe alignment rather than forcing trades out of FOMO.
The technical requirement in an ascending market that a higher high ($HH$) must be followed by a higher low ($HL$).
The technical requirement in a descending market that a lower high ($LH$) must be followed by a lower low ($LL$).
The practice of clearing chart noise by visually pinpointing structural pivots based exclusively on the last 1 to 3 trading sessions.
